creator: Alexander Terp
description:
The owner asked on 2026-11-20 (chat note) whether Muster could parse every message between the person and an agent, and every tool call, so that the back-and-forth in a pane could be reconstructed elsewhere, such as in the Foreman app.

It looks possible without reading the screen. Claude Code appends each turn to `~/.claude/projects/<dir>/<session>.jsonl` (user and assistant messages, tool calls and results, subagent and compaction records) and Codex writes a rollout file under `~/.codex/sessions/`. Both hand its path to every hook as `transcript_path`, which Muster's adapters already receive and read today only for context, effort and compaction. The daemon could tail a pane's transcript and serve a stream of messages and tool calls in Muster's own vocabulary through the API (MIP-10), so Foreman or a conversation view could draw it, on a remote machine too.

Open: these formats are each harness's internals and change without notice, so each needs a corpus recording and a check in its harness tier; OpenCode keeps history in a database, not a file; transcripts carry secrets, so the stream needs the same care as the run log's rule about typed text. Direction undecided, so this is an idea, not committed work.
title: Reconstruct each agent's conversation and tool calls from its harness transcript
